blocks.p: A newspaper opens in a reader, and a notebook opens as a page to write on. Figure 39-1 shows a notebook open at its first page, with the list of its pages at the left.

caption: Figure 39-1
A notebook open at its first page.

blocks.p: The *Pages* list at the left shows the first line of each page, or *Blank* for a page with nothing on it; the page shown is marked. A page holds 15 lines and 1,200 letters; the count under its lines gives what is used, here *5 of 15 lines* and *198 of 1,200 letters*. At the foot of the window are *Erase page*, *Lock*, the arrows that turn the pages, and *Done*.

marks.text: The Pages list shows the first line of each page, or Blank.
A page has a title, lines to write on and its page number.

sticky.text: A notebook opens as a page to write on.

blocks.p: Figure 39-2 shows a newspaper in the reader. The side column at the right tells what the piece is, its date and whether it has been read, and lists the stories on the page.

caption: Figure 39-2
A newspaper in the reader, with its side column, zoom buttons and switch shown closer.

blocks.p: Choose *Paper* to see the page as it was printed, or *Words* to read the same text in plain type.

marks.text: The side column lists the stories. Pick one to jump to it.
Zoom the printed page with the buttons at the foot.
Paper shows the page as printed. Words shows the same text in plain type.

sticky.text: A newspaper opens in a reader.
